answer: Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the voyage registry records each claim and the haven audit publishes every slash. Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 33% of the attester's bond. A farm must therefore either lie, which the ledge graph proves on replay, or recruit 12 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. That is 12 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
